Rock of Our Salvation
rok uhv owr sal-VAY-shuhn
noun
From Psalm 95:1 and Deuteronomy 32; a title of the LORD as the strong, faithful ground of His people’s deliverance.

Biblical Definition

The Rock of our salvation is a title of the LORD as the strong, faithful, and unchanging ground of His people’s deliverance. The psalmist calls the people to worship: O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. The Song of Moses extols Him: He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. The title gathers up several truths: the LORD is a rock for strength, an unshakable refuge in whom His people take shelter from every storm; a rock for stability, the unchanging God who is the same yesterday, today, and for ever; and a rock for salvation, the sure foundation of their deliverance, who has wrought their redemption and will not let it fail. Against the rock of the LORD, the gods of the nations are no rock at all, as Moses sang: their rock is not as our Rock. In the New Testament this Rock is revealed as Christ, the horn of salvation raised up for His people. The dictionary honors the Rock of our salvation as a name of comfort and confidence: that the believer’s deliverance rests not upon the sand of his own strength but upon the strong, faithful, eternal God, whose work is perfect and whose salvation cannot be moved.

A title of the LORD as the strong, faithful, unchanging ground of His people’s deliverance; the Rock whose work is perfect, revealed in Christ.

Key Scripture

Psa 95:1 — "O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation."

Deu 32:4 — "He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he."

Psa 62:2 — "He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved."

Modern Corruption

Salvation’s ground is shifted to human strength or effort; Scripture names the LORD the Rock of our salvation, the strong and faithful ground that cannot be moved.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the perennial instinct to shift the ground of salvation from the LORD to ourselves—to rest deliverance on our own strength, resolve, or works, building on the sand of human ability rather than the Rock. Every such refuge fails when the storm comes; the gods of the nations and the idols of the self are no rock, as Moses sang, their rock is not as our Rock.

The principle to recover is that the LORD Himself is the Rock of our salvation, the strong and faithful ground that cannot be moved. He is the Rock, His work is perfect, and all His ways are judgment (Deu 32:4): His salvation is no half-finished, failing thing, but a perfect work. He only is the believer’s rock and salvation, his defence; he shall not be greatly moved (Psa 62:2). So the psalmist calls the people to worship Him with joy: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation (Psa 95:1). This Rock is revealed in Christ, the horn of salvation; and the believer who builds his hope upon Him, and not upon himself, stands secure when every other ground gives way.
